tagline: Self-hosted web music streamer that serves your own audio files, built on Laravel and Vue.
description: Koel scans a folder of music you already own and serves it through a browser player. It handles playlists, smart playlists, podcasts, radio, scrobbling, and links to Last.fm, Spotify and MusicBrainz. The core is MIT-licensed. The server is a Laravel application that needs PHP 8.2 or newer and a database: MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL and SQLite have all been tested. The docs describe five install methods, including a standalone archive that bundles FrankenPHP and defaults to SQLite, so a host needs no system PHP. Official iOS and Android apps live in a separate repository, Koel Player. A paid tier called Koel Plus adds multi-user libraries, collaboration, single sign-on, cloud storage drivers, custom themes and white-labeling. Koel can replace Spotify Premium only for a personal collection. It does not come with a licensed catalogue, so every track must be a file you supply yourself.
strengths: Standalone binary with SQLite by default, so a host needs no PHP, Composer or Node install.
Supports MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL and SQLite as databases.
Smart playlists, podcasts and radio sit next to the music library in one web interface.
Official mobile app, Koel Player, covers iOS and Android.
Scrobbling and Last.fm, Spotify and MusicBrainz integrations are built in.
limits: No music catalogue: it streams only files you already own, so it does not replace discovery on Spotify.
Multi-user libraries, collaboration, single sign-on, cloud storage drivers and white-labeling require the paid Koel Plus.
The mobile app is a separate project from the server, with its own repository.
Running from source needs PHP 8.2, Composer, Node.js 20 and pnpm.
bestFor: A music collector with a home server who wants a browser and phone player for a personal library.
